page.layout: One page of text. Above the text: a centred title block (DE SOCINO / ET / SOCINIANISMO / Dissertatio.) under a woodcut ornament, then the heading ARGUMENTUM. Below that: one paragraph beginning with a large woodcut initial O, running to the foot. Bottom: signature "A" at left, catchword "consensu" at right. No margin notes.

l.i: compegerit, novamque sectam de suo instituerit. Artes
quibus usus est, in Dogmatibus suis uniusque
Opportunitates item, quas sedulo Idem arripuit, ad
Hæreses suas disseminandas, præsertim in Polonia.
Ejusdem superbia summa, & arrogantia, dum suo
ipsius ingenio in omnibus fidit; & Amicorum Judicia
vilipendit; neque hoc contentus, Catholicam Ecclesiam
contemnit; eamque non suæ solius ætatis, sed & seculi Primitivi,

page.notes: Top right corner shows faint mirrored text ("De Socino ..."), which is show-through from the other side and was left out. The page number at top centre is in brackets; the final digit is uncertain, so it is marked [?]. The initial O is a woodcut; its word is joined as "Origo". "Lalio" and "uniusque" are read from a small, heavy print and may be imprecise. The line "uniustujusque" in the scan appears to be a printing or ligature artefact; I read it as "uniusque".
